profile_text.body:
Credo AI describes itself as an AI governance platform company, founded in 2020, that created the AI governance category and is now defining it for the agentic era. According to its site, the platform is built on a Knowledge Graph that fuses global regulatory intelligence with a customer's business context, and it is intended to help enterprises discover their AI, enforce policy, manage AI risk, and achieve what the company calls Measurable Trust across every agent, application, model, and AI vendor. The company says it offers governance at the model, application, and agent level, with agents treated as first-class governed entities that are registered, risk-assessed, sanctioned, and governed. It also describes GAIA (Govern AI Assistant) as generally available in the platform.

The site says Credo AI provides ready-to-deploy policy packs covering the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, and other standards, written by a team it says has worked with ISO, NIST, the EU Parliament, NATO, and OECD. It cites native integrations across existing systems and says its regulatory intelligence draws on 300+ integrations and forward-deployed governance experts. The site states that the platform was built from scratch for governance rather than added onto a GRC tool, and it includes customer statements attributed to Mastercard and IBM, among others, describing uses such as managing AI risk, implementing generative AI, and accelerating EU AI Act compliance.

The company's tracked product is the Credo AI platform itself, listed under AI Governance and Risk Management Platforms, with a note describing purpose-built AI governance, policy packs for the EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF, a clean interface, and fast deployment. No lawsuits or MCP servers are recorded for the company.
